input: Apply for a remote work stipend from my employer

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The stipend could cover a wide range of things (internet, equipment, furniture, co-working space) — knowing what is included shapes what to request and justify.
Whether a formal application process already exists at the employer (a portal, a form, an email request) determines how much the user needs to create vs. follow an existing path.
Knowing who owns this process (HR, a direct manager, finance) tells the user who to contact first and whose approval is needed.
There may be eligibility requirements (tenure, role type, location) or a cap on the stipend amount that the user needs to verify before applying.
The user may need to gather specific supporting documents (receipts, invoices, proof of home-office setup) before they can submit anything.
Success could mean a one-time reimbursement, a recurring monthly allowance, or a direct equipment purchase — the target outcome affects the strategy.
The user may want to prioritise certain expenses (e.g., ergonomic furniture vs. faster internet) if the stipend has a spending limit, which shapes how they frame the request.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for employer remote work stipend
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to successfully apply for a remote work stipend offered by their employer, which likely involves understanding eligibility, gathering documentation, and submitting a formal request.

questions.title: What expenses does the stipend cover at your company?
questions.description: Clarify whether the stipend is for internet, equipment, furniture, co-working space, or a combination, so the application scope is accurate.

questions.title: Does your employer have an existing application process or form?
questions.description: Determine whether there is an official portal, HR form, or email process already in place, or whether the user needs to initiate a request from scratch.

questions.title: Who do you submit the stipend request to?
questions.description: Identify the right point of contact — HR department, direct manager, or finance team — to ensure the request reaches the correct approver.

questions.title: Are there eligibility requirements you need to meet first?
questions.description: Check for conditions such as minimum tenure, full-time status, role type, or geographic location that could affect whether the user qualifies.

questions.title: Do you need receipts or documentation to support the request?
questions.description: Find out whether the application requires proof of purchases, invoices, or a home-office setup description before submission.

questions.title: Is the stipend a one-time payment or a recurring allowance?
questions.description: Understand whether the user is applying for a single reimbursement or an ongoing monthly benefit, as this changes the framing and urgency of the application.

questions.title: Which expense category is your highest priority to cover?
questions.description: If the stipend has a spending cap, knowing whether internet, furniture, or equipment matters most lets the user frame their request most effectively.
